resources.string: After the tablet sleeps for 4 hours or more on battery, BooxUltimatum posts a short notification with how much battery it used and anything unusual. It also says when the battery ran out. It needs permission to show notifications and shows nothing without it.
Notifications are blocked for BooxUltimatum, so the report can’t appear. Allow them in Android’s settings.
No sleep of 4 hours or more in the last 48 hours.
Couldn’t read the log just now.
Switch off a display that stays on

If the display stays on while the tablet is asleep, which can drain the battery overnight, BooxUltimatum tries to switch it off. It starts after 2 minutes, tries again after 5, 10, 20 and 40 minutes, then tries every hour until the display goes off.\nEach try runs five steps and stops at the first that works. It asks the Boox sleep screen to refresh, tells it the display is on, locks the screen, wakes the tablet and locks it again, and presses the wake and sleep buttons. The two steps that lock the screen need BooxUltimatum’s accessibility service, and the last needs Shizuku. Without them those steps are skipped. The log records each step’s result. None has been seen to work yet on a Note Air6 C.
Refresh the sleep screen while asleep

While the tablet sleeps, BooxUltimatum asks the sleep screen to refresh every 30 minutes if nothing else has. On a Note Air6 C, after Android restarted by itself, the display stayed on overnight and drained the battery each time 90 minutes passed without a refresh. A refresh costs well under 1 mAh a night. This is a precaution against that pattern, not a proven cure.
Switch off a display that stays on (experimental): %1$s, and the display went to sleep.
The attempt to switch off the display failed (experimental): the display stayed on.

Android restarted by itself, and the tablet hasn’t been restarted since. On a Note Air6 C, the processor then stayed awake during sleep and used several times as much battery. Twice, the display also stayed on all night and drained the battery. A restart cleared both. Restart the tablet before you leave it asleep: hold the power button, then tap Restart.
The processor stayed awake while the tablet slept

The tablet’s processor stayed awake through a sleep of %1$s, which uses several times as much battery as a normal sleep. On a Note Air6 C, this state can leave the display on all night, and restarting the tablet has cleared it each time. Hold the power button, then tap Restart.
An app kept the tablet awake while it slept
The tablet’s processor stayed awake through a sleep of %1$s because an app held it awake. Open Battery › Causes to see which one.
